stemMd: Which of these European capital cities stands on the river Danube?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** Several of these cities are capitals of countries that lie in the Danube's basin or along its course, so knowing the country is not enough. The question is about the river that runs through the city itself.

**The fact that settles it.** The Danube rises in the Black Forest in Germany and flows east to the Black Sea. On the way it passes through four capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade. Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia, stands on the Danube right beside the borders with Austria and Hungary.

**How to check it.** Give each of the other cities its own river. Prague stands on the Vltava, Zagreb on the Sava, Warsaw on the Vistula and Bucharest on the Dambovita. None of those is the Danube, so Bratislava is the only one left.

distractorRationale.b: Romania is a Danube country - the river forms much of its southern border with Bulgaria and reaches the Black Sea through a delta that lies mostly in Romania - so it is tempting to place its capital on the river too. But Bucharest stands on the Dambovita, well north of the Danube.
distractorRationale.a: Prague is a great river city, which makes it feel like a Danube capital, but its river is the Vltava, which flows into the Elbe and on to the North Sea. The Danube does not flow through the Czech Republic at all.
distractorRationale.c: Zagreb stands on the Sava, which is a tributary of the Danube and joins it at Belgrade. Being on a tributary puts Zagreb in the Danube basin, not on the Danube itself.
distractorRationale.d: Warsaw stands on the Vistula, which flows north to the Baltic Sea. It belongs to a different river system altogether; Poland is not crossed by the Danube.

accessibilityText: Question: which of these European capital cities stands on the river Danube? The choices are Prague, Bucharest, Zagreb, Warsaw and Bratislava.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section (geography). The distractors are capitals of Danube-basin or Danube-bordering countries and a capital on a Danube tributary, so the item tests placing the city, not the country.

review.author: wave6-polito-til-a-genknow-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Bratislava is on the Danube. Prague is on the Vltava, Zagreb on the Sava, Warsaw on the Vistula, and Bucharest on the Dambovita, well away from the Danube. Only one Danube capital is offered. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: The Danube runs through Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade. Bucharest lies on the Dambovita, about 60 km from the Danube, which makes it the strong distractor, but it is not on the river. Prague is on the Vltava, Zagreb on the Sava and Warsaw on the Vistula.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the capitals on the Danube are Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade; of the five choices only Bratislava is among them. Bucharest (Dambovita), Prague (Vltava), Zagreb (Sava) and Warsaw (Vistula) each stand on another river. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
